# Safe code review: Safenet audit-log step

The change is in good shape. Fix one timeline bug before opening the PR; everything else is small.

Mode: full review, limited to committed changes in `a9c863e…HEAD`, read-only. The merge-base is `37e10732`, so the review covers exactly one commit, `8006ed77a`. 17 files, +581 −9.

The repo is the Safe{Wallet} monorepo (TypeScript, Next.js web plus shared `packages/`). Tests run on Jest, and lint, type-check and prettier run through Turbo. I found 5 stated rules in `AGENTS.md` and `apps/web/AGENTS.md` that apply here: the feature architecture, feature flags, a Storybook story for every new component, tests for all new logic, and treating comments as debt. All 9 review areas had something to check.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Fix F1, then open the PR |
| **Score** | **93 / 100** (2 of 6 findings checked by a confirm agent and a refute agent) |
| **Held the score down** | A break in the audit-log timeline while a transaction still needs signatures |
| **Fix first** | F1 in `TxSigners/index.tsx:270,281` |

## Scores by area, worst first
| Area | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Bugs | 88 | F1 |
| Testing | 92 | F4 |
| Conventions | 92 | F3, F6 |
| DRY | 95 | F2 |
| Performance | 96 | F5 |
| Security, regression, architecture, KISS | 100 | nothing found |

## Must fix before opening

**F1 · P2 · Bugs · confirmed by both agents** (`apps/web/src/components/transactions/TxSigners/index.tsx:270`, `:281`, `:287`)
- **What:** The new Safenet row sits between the signature rows and the execution row. The creation and signature rows still decide whether they are the last row by checking only `!showExecutionRow`, and never ask whether the Safenet row will render.
- **What the user sees:** Take a transaction that is still collecting signatures (`showExecutionRow` is false) and already has a Safenet check. A check starts as soon as the transaction is proposed (`deriveCheckState.ts:93`). The last signature row, or the creation row if nobody has signed, is marked last. `AuditRow` then leaves out its connector line (`AuditLog/index.tsx:118`), and the Safenet step appears below it, cut off from the timeline.
- **Fix:** Work out whether the Safenet row is visible in `TxSigners` and feed that into the earlier rows' `isLast`. The row only renders when a check exists, so this probably means reading `useSafenetCheck` there too, or moving the visibility check into a small hook the feature exports.

## Worth a ticket or a quick fix

| ID | Pri | Area | Location | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F2 | P3 | DRY | `apps/web/src/features/safenet-checks/components/SafenetAuditRow.tsx:78` (and `packages/store/src/safenet/safenetCheckApi.ts:50`) | The component repeats the API's rule for choosing the attestation event (oracle first, plain as fallback). Its comment says it links "the same event the api verifies", but nothing in the code keeps the two in step. Today they match. If one side changes, the link could point to a transaction other than the one that was verified. Put the tx hash of the chosen attestation on the snapshot, or share one `selectAttestedEvent` helper. *Confirmed by both agents, lowered to minor impact.* |
| F3 | P3 | Conventions | `apps/web/src/features/safenet-checks/components/SafenetAuditRow.tsx:1` | This new component has no `.stories.tsx`, which `apps/web/AGENTS.md:10` and `:148` require. Its five statuses, and the new `actor` / `iconColor` props on `AuditRow`, are only visible in tests. |
| F4 | P3 | Testing | `apps/web/src/components/transactions/TxSigners/index.test.tsx` | The new tests only cover the Safenet row alongside a normal execution row. Nothing covers a transaction still awaiting signatures that has a Safenet row, which is the case where F1 happens. The dark-mode `iconColor` mapping (`SafenetAuditRow.tsx:32`) is also untested. |
| F5 | P3 | Performance | `packages/store/src/safenet/safenetCheckApi.ts:53-59` | The comment says the block-header read costs "one RPC per settled check". In practice `blockTimeMs` runs on every poll that sees an attestation event. That includes polls every 6s while the status is waiting for verification (group key not ready yet) and every refetch after the 300s cache expires. The cost is bounded by the deadline plus the late window, so this is small. Also, when the header read fails, the reader tries each RPC endpoint in turn (`safenetReader.ts:447`), which delays the verdict for that poll. Either read the header only once the status is `BENIGN` or `MALICIOUS`, or fix the comment. |
| F6 | P3 | Conventions | `packages/utils/src/features/safenet-checks/constants.ts:54` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SAFENET_EXPLORER_URL` is read here but is missing from `apps/web/.env.example`. This diff documents every other Safenet variable there (`.env.example:5-31`). |

## Checked and ruled out
- **Hand-rolled `FeatureHandle` instead of `createFeatureHandle`** (`features/safenet-checks/index.ts:15`): the repo already does this in `actions-tray` and `ledger`. It is needed here for the `SAFENET_CHECKS_FORCE` override.
- **Security:** link URLs are built from the tx hash in the chain log, the Safe's own `chainId`, and a URL from config. The link only appears on `BENIGN`, which requires a FROST-verified attestation. `ExternalLink` handles `rel`. No problem found.
- **Regression:** the new `AuditRow` props are optional and additive, and the new row sits behind the flag. The test with the flag off confirms nothing reads the chain.
- **Comment density:** heavy, but it matches the existing Safenet code (`safenetCheckApi.ts`, `useSafenetCheck.ts`), so I didn't file it.

## What this review did not cover
- 4 of the 6 findings (F3 to F6) were not checked by agents. They count at full weight in the score.
- I didn't run tests, lint or type-check, and I didn't render the UI. F1 comes from reading the code, not from seeing it on screen.
- There is no "since your last run" section: none was found, and nothing was recorded because this run was read-only.
- No cleanup proposals and nothing applied, since this was read-only.

## How this was produced
I resolved the scope, profiled the repo, and ran all 9 area passes. For F1 and F2, one agent tried to confirm each finding and another tried to refute it; both findings survived. Scores come from the Safe review scoring model.
